constraint_table.explanation: Large theta23 suggests a quasi-degenerate 2-3 modal sector.
Moderate theta12 is easier to obtain from a one-plus-two modal decomposition than from a fully rigid hierarchy.
Small but nonzero theta13 points to weak singlet-doublet coupling rather than exact decoupling.
Exact degeneracy must be lifted, but only moderately, to avoid destroying the atmospheric sector.
Closed geometries naturally support shared branch modes and coherent recirculation.
A twisted or nontrivial closed topology is a plausible way to keep theta23 large while preventing theta13 from blowing up.
Charged leptons remain more hierarchical than neutrinos in the toy layer.
The atmospheric sector is naturally read as a collective branch/doublet effect.

notes: This is an inverse-structure inference, not a proof of uniqueness.
Weights rank how strongly a PMNS-like target suggests each structural feature.
